Let's craft final answer answer.<|end_think|>Let  

\[
\vec A,\;\vec B,\;\vec C,\;\vec D\in\mathbb R^{2}
\]

be the position vectors of the vertices of \(ABCD\) taken in order.

Reflecting a point about another point means the second point is the
mid‑point of the segment joining the original point and its image.
Hence  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\vec E&=2\vec B-\vec A,\\[2pt]
\vec F&=2\vec C-\vec B,\\[2pt]
\vec G&=2\vec D-\vec C,\\[2pt]
\vec H&=2\vec A-\vec D .
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 1.  Signed area of a polygon

For vertices \(P_{1},P_{2},\dots ,P_{n}\) taken consecutively, the signed
area is  

\[
[\,P_{1}P_{2}\dots P_{n}\,]=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^{n}
\bigl(\vec P_i\times\vec P_{i+1}\bigr) ,
\qquad 
\vec P_{n+1}= \vec P_{1},
\]

where \(\vec u\times\vec v=x_1y_2-y_1x_2\) is the 2‑D scalar cross product.

Thus  

\[
[ABCD]=\frac12\bigl(\vec A\times\vec B+\vec B\times\vec C
+\vec C\times\vec D+\vec D\times\vec A\bigr).
\tag{2}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2.  Area of \(EFGH\)

Insert the expressions (1) into the shoelace sum for \(EFGH\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
\Sigma&=
\vec E\times\vec F+\vec F\times\vec G+\vec G\times\vec H+\vec H\times\vec E \\
&=(2\vec B-\vec A)\times(2\vec C-\vec B)
 +(2\vec C-\vec B)\times(2\vec D-\vec C)\\
&\qquad+(2\vec D-\vec C)\times(2\vec A-\vec D)
 +(2\vec A-\vec D)\times(2\vec B-\vec A).
\end{aligned}
\]

Expanding each product and using \(\vec X\times\vec X=0\) gives  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\Sigma
=&\;4\vec B\times\vec C-2\vec A\times\vec C+\vec A\times\vec B\\
&+4\vec C\times\vec D-2\vec B\times\vec D+\vec B\times\vec C\\
&+4\vec D\times\vec A-2\vec C\times\vec A+\vec C\times\vec D\\
&+4\vec A\times\vec B-2\vec D\times\vec B+\vec D\times\vec A .
\end{aligned}
\]

Group the like terms:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\Sigma
=&\;5(\vec A\times\vec B+\vec B\times\vec C+\vec C\times\vec D+\vec D\times\vec A)\\[2pt]
&\;-\underbrace{2\vec A\times\vec C-2\vec C\times\vec A}_{=0}
   -\underbrace{2\vec B\times\vec D-2\vec D\times\vec B}_{=0}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Hence  

\[
\Sigma =5\bigl(\vec A\times\vec B+\vec B\times\vec C+\vec C\times\vec D+\vec D\times\vec A\bigr).
\]

The signed area of \(EFGH\) is  

\[
[EFGH]=\frac12\Sigma
      =\frac12\cdot5\bigl(\vec A\times\vec B+\vec B\times\vec C
      +\vec C\times\vec D+\vec D\times\vec A\bigr)
      =5\,[ABCD].
\tag{3}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 3.  Ratio of the areas

Equation (3) shows that, for any non‑degenerate quadrilateral,

\[
\frac{[ABCD]}{[EFGH]}=\frac{1}{5}=0.20.
\]

Thus the quadrilateral \(ABCD\) occupies exactly **20 %** of the area of
\(EFGH\).
